author: Copilot
body: `refresh_access_token` defaults to copying `account_licenses` from the refresh token payload when the caller doesn’t explicitly pass `account_licenses`. For MCP tokens, refresh tokens can be valid for a long time (currently 30 days), so a license downgrade/removal would not be enforced for the remaining refresh-token lifetime (refresh keeps re-minting tokens with the old license set). Consider requiring callers to supply current licenses at refresh time (and failing/omitting the claim if not supplied), or otherwise ensuring MCP refresh cannot perpetuate stale license entitlements.

author: Copilot
body:
`_enabled_account_licenses()` returns a `set`, and the token claim is then built by iterating that set. Set iteration order is not deterministic, so the `account_licenses` list embedded into the JWT can vary across requests for the same license state (making tokens harder to compare/debug and risking flaky assertions if more licenses are enabled). Build the list in a deterministic order (e.g., iterate `AccountLicenseKey` in enum order and filter, or sort the enabled keys before serializing).
```suggestion
            "account_licenses": [
                license_key.value
                for license_key in sorted(_enabled_account_licenses(account_license), key=lambda license_key: license_key.value)
            ],
```

author: Copilot
body: `account_licenses` is preserved by copying it out of the *refresh token* and re-embedding it into newly minted tokens. Since MCP refresh tokens are configured for a long lifetime (30 days), this can keep premium entitlements active long after a license downgrade/revocation until the user fully re-authorizes. Consider re-resolving current account licenses during refresh (preferred) or shortening the refresh-token lifetime / forcing re-auth when license claims are missing or stale, so license changes take effect promptly.

author: Copilot
body: `verify_token` validates the access token via `mcp_refresh_tracking_service.validate_access_token(token)` but then immediately re-parses the same JWT via `client_factory.claims_from_token(token)`. Since `validate_access_token` already returns `PortalTokenClaimsBody`, consider using its return value as `claims` to avoid duplicate parsing and keep a single source of truth for the claims used later (e.g., `claims.exp`).

author: Copilot
body:
MCP-side license caching can extend entitlement staleness beyond the upstream WebAPI license cache. Here `license_ttl = min(session_settings.license_cache_ttl_seconds, token_ttl)` (default 3600s) may keep `account_licenses` valid for up to an hour, even though WebAPI’s `AccountRepo.get_account_license()` is already tenant-cached for 10 minutes (`cache_time_settings.ttl_medium`).

Consider capping `license_ttl` to the upstream license TTL (or lowering the default `LICENSE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`) so revoked license bits stop authorizing tools sooner.

author: Copilot
body: The PR description says MCP-specific tokens will include `account_licenses` in JWT claims and that token creation/refresh flows propagate those claims, but the implementation and this README section describe licenses being resolved dynamically from Web API instead of embedded in JWT claims. Please reconcile (update PR description or add the missing claim propagation) so the PR matches the intended design.

author: Copilot
body: `verify_token()` decodes JWT claims but never enforces `aud == "mcp"` when both permission and license caches hit. That means the intended “MCP-only token” restriction is bypassed on cache hit (and could also be bypassed via cache poisoning). Validate the audience immediately after `claims_from_token()` (or switch to `build_client_and_claims_from_token()` so audience is always checked) before returning an `AccessToken`.

body: The PR description states that `account_licenses` is added to MCP token/JWT claims and propagated through mint/refresh, but this README describes permissions/licenses being resolved dynamically in MCP rather than embedded in JWT claims. Please align the PR description and documentation (either update the description or adjust docs if JWT claim embedding is actually intended).
